summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT). Embedded software engineer with C++ and Python experience across STM32 bare-metal firmware, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson, spanning UART and I2C sensor integration to real-time ML inference on edge hardware. Owned a voice-controlled robotic arm end to end over a three-layer distributed pipeline, debugging 11 integration failures to reach 100% pick reliability.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Built a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID cursor commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Designed a custom wavelet bank (alpha-blended sym6+bior3.5) to suppress low-frequency noise; combined with optimized homography stitching, bit manipulation, and concurrency to achieve a PSNR of 86.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization; used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions; designed single-layer PCBs in EAGLE and implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place system over a three-layer distributed pipeline: Flutter mobile client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller linked by a unified WebSocket fabric.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection via dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over an I2C mux.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver on Cortex-M4.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Achieved up to 30x speedup with static strip partitioning (55 processes); demonstrated that a dynamic task queue outperformed all static methods under unpredictable workloads.
Implemented and benchmarked four parallel work-distribution strategies (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) for rendering 5000x5000 pixel scenes using MPI.
